# Shape icon fixtures and regression scope

`vision-round-two-initial.png` is a byte-for-byte copy of the local read-only
MuMu/WGC capture
`compatibility_probe/artifacts/20260930T141039Z_53baa46b/latest.png`.
No input was generated by this shape investigation. The user manually changed
to the second round before the capture.

The captured frame is 1924x1142, including the window chrome. Its HUD shows
round 2 and 45/45 remaining board cells. The three visible quantity labels
are 1, 2, and 5. Those quantities do not determine the shape dimensions.
The shape badges independently contain **4x2, 4x1, and 3x1** dark squares.

| Real fixture | SHA-256 | Observed shapes | Covered cells |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vision-round-two-initial.png` | `857dd560addebbfc9cb89cd695d01c898029a438b4ed854777c33b09e7f34eae` | 4x2, 4x1, 3x1 | 45/45 |
| `vision-initial.png` | `edc3f8bb0b1fe407b23007dab4f375f2a469d98e710cb7d681159230271d3b60` | 3x2, 3x1, 2x1 | 45/45 |

The preceding-round image is the existing real fixture; its original source
and board evidence remain documented in `vision-fixtures.md`. It has not
been regenerated or modified.

At the production sampler's normalized 42x32 badge resolution, the second
round's accepted connected-component statistics are:

| Card | Components | Pixel areas | Component widths | Component heights | Light pixels |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| 0 | 8 | 28..34 | 5..6 | 6 | 916 |
| 1 | 4 | 29..34 | 5..6 | 6 | 1025 |
| 2 | 3 | 42..45 | 6..7 | 7 | 1028 |

Before the repair, all three cards supplied recognized badge anchors, but
the allowed dimension range 1..3 rejected the two four-column icons. The
observed shapes were `[0,0], [0,0], [3,1]`. The repair retains the RGB and
relative-brightness thresholds, and reads dimensions only from badge pixels.
There is no fixed 4x4 item limit: an observed rectangle is geometrically
possible when either orientation fits the existing 9x5 board.

`vision_shapes` exercises the actual `Recognizer::analyze` implementation:

- Two real round fixtures retain all 45 covered labels, three ready card
  references, and their existing board geometry.
- The real second-round viewport is also resized to 1920x1080, 1440x810,
  and 960x540, using the same fixture-only resizing approach as prior tests.
- One generated-icon test contains all 16 dimensions in 1..4 by 1..4,
  rendered into all three badge slots while preserving their different real
  card art. A dense 4x4 mask reaches normalized y=3..28; both extreme rows
  must be counted completely. The card-art fingerprints remain unchanged.
- Larger generated 5x1, 1x5, 5x5, 8x5, and 5x6 badges must also be read;
  5x6 fits the board only after rotation. A complete 6x6 grid inside the
  badge region must remain unknown because neither orientation fits 9x5.
- Negative controls retain visible pixels from a square beyond each search
  edge, remove one corner square, add a malformed dark component, place more
  rows/columns than the board can hold, repeat row/column intersections, or remove the
  badge squares and leave only noise. These must return `[0,0]` for that
  card while retaining the other two cards' observed dimensions.

The generated badges are bounded parser regressions, not captures from a
different activity, and do not prove cross-activity or physical 4x4-item
acceptance. A completely removed row/column can become visually identical
to a smaller complete icon; no test claims to detect pixels that are absent.
Sampling remains bounded to the actual 42x32 badge and its interior. Squares
smaller than the unchanged three-pixel side / six-pixel area threshold,
merged dark components, or pixels beyond that region cannot establish a
complete icon. This resolution limit can leave a dense geometrically valid
item unknown; it is not a fixed business limit on item dimensions.
The dynamic orientation helper separately tests 1x9/9x1 and 5x9/9x5, filtering
each direction by the board instead of rejecting the unrotated dimensions.
Host OCR, quantity reading, round epochs, the solver, and native output are
verified separately by the main task. This target does not play or advance
the game and does not alter existing recognition test expectations.

## Verified checks

The source state containing this repair passed:

`cargo test --test vision_shapes --test vision_recognition --test vision_dynamic --test vision_sparse_board -- --nocapture`

Results: `vision_shapes` 16/16, `vision_recognition` 22/22,
`vision_dynamic` 12/12, and `vision_sparse_board` 12/12. There are **47 unique
cases**, comprising the previous 35, 11 new independent shape cases, and one
new orientation case. The five shared module cases execute in each target,
so 62 successful test executions must not be reported as 62 unique cases.
Compiler output contains only unused-field/method warnings from the
integration-target imports. The transcript is saved at
`.artifacts/round-shapes/test-output.txt` in the workspace.
